papers.title: Artificial intelligence and radiomics in small cell lung cancer: a narrative review of imaging and multisource data integration.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and radiomics are increasingly used to analyze imaging and multisource data in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the directness and clinical maturity of the available evidence remain uncertain. This narrative review aimed to summarize and critically evaluate SCLC-specific, mixed-cohort, and indirect evidence across diagnostic classification, prognostic prediction, treatment-associated outcomes, and lesion segmentation.
papers.summary: This narrative review critically evaluates the current state of AI and radiomics applications in small cell lung cancer, covering diagnostic classification, prognosis prediction, treatment outcomes, and lesion segmentation. The authors assess the directness and clinical maturity of SCLC-specific versus mixed-cohort and indirect evidence, highlighting gaps between research promise and clinical readiness.

papers.title: PCA-mapping and machine learning identify multiple chemotypes with antiplasmodial, β-haematin and haemozoin formation inhibition activity.
papers.abstract: Inhibiting the formation of haemozoin remains a robust, non-genomic target for antiplasmodial drug discovery. While current efforts focus on multistage active compounds that are not pure haemozoin formation inhibitors, this class offers advantages including selectivity for Plasmodium and is associated with lowered resistance risks. With a view to developing cost-effective tools to streamline the discovery process, we developed a high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) workflow integrating both ligand- and structure-based techniques. Here, we employed a principal component analysis (PCA) enric
papers.summary: This study developed a high-throughput virtual screening workflow combining ligand- and structure-based methods, including PCA-based mapping and machine learning, to identify compounds that inhibit haemozoin formation as a strategy against malaria. The approach uncovered multiple chemotypes with antiplasmodial activity and β-haematin/haemozoin formation inhibition, offering a cost-effective way to streamline antimalarial drug discovery.

papers.title: CDKPredict: a clinicogenomic model for risk-adapted therapeutic intervention in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Wide variation in outcomes is observed for patients with hormone-receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer (MBC) receiving first-line CDK4/6 inhibitors plus endocrine therapy (CDK4/6i+ET). Although front-line escalation strategies are beginning to enter clinical practice, assigning patients to intensified or de-intensified approaches remains challenging due to several mechanisms of resistance spanning tumor-intrinsic and host factors. To address this, we developed CDKPredict, an interpretable machine-learning model integrating baseline clinicopathologic and genomic features to predict outcome
papers.summary: CDKPredict is an interpretable machine-learning model that combines baseline clinical, pathologic, and genomic features to predict outcomes for patients with hormone-receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer receiving first-line CDK4/6 inhibitors plus endocrine therapy. The model aims to help clinicians decide which patients should receive intensified versus de-intensified treatment, addressing the challenge of variable responses driven by multiple resistance mechanisms.

papers.title: Disease relevance and replicability of deep learning gene expression prediction.
papers.abstract: Recent deep learning (DL) models predict average gene expression levels from DNA sequences with high overall correlation to measured values. We examine these DL models through the lens of disease research. The seemingly high overall performance of DL models is largely due to capturing whether genes are "On" or "Off", and to a lesser extent, disease-relevant expression level changes for "On" genes. Indeed, the more bimodal the gene expression distribution, the better the reported performance. We track the extent of this issue across tissues, molecular systems, and cancers. Compounding the model
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint evaluates deep learning models that predict gene expression from DNA sequence, showing that their high overall correlation largely reflects simply distinguishing whether genes are 'on' or 'off' rather than accurately predicting disease-relevant expression level changes. Performance is inflated for genes with bimodal expression distributions, and this limitation is tracked across tissues, molecular systems, and cancers, raising concerns about the models' replicability and utility for disease research.

papers.title: Biological rationales from language models enable leakage-resistant forecasts of target-indication success.
papers.abstract: Identifying which target-indication (T-I) hypotheses can translate into clinical success remains a central challenge in drug discovery. We present PRIORITI (Prospective Rationale-Informed Outcome Reasoning for Integrated Target-indication Intelligence), a leakage-resistant framework that separates upstream biological evidence synthesis from outcome prediction. Given only a target gene and disease indication, a domain-instructed large language model (LLM) synthesizes drug-agnostic human genetics across prespecified channels. These evidence were embedded and combined with static entity context d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PRIORITI, a framework that uses a domain-instructed large language model to synthesize drug-agnostic biological evidence for a given target-indication pair, then predicts clinical success from these rationales in a leakage-resistant manner. By separating evidence synthesis from outcome prediction, the approach aims to avoid information leakage that can inflate performance in target-indication forecasting. This offers a potentially more realistic way to prioritize drug targets before clinical trials.

papers.title: AI-Based Comparison of UniProt annotations and Literature Across Human Kinases.
papers.abstract: Curated protein records and their supporting publications organize biological evidence at different levels of detail. Here, we used AI to independently answer a set of biological questions using either UniProt records or the full texts of the literature cited by those records, and then used AI-based evaluation to compare the resulting answers in terms of information coverage and semantic agreement. Fifty human proteins were selected from ten groups in a kinase sequence collection. Target-identity filtering retained 1,749 protein-publication records representing 1,655 distinct publications. For
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses AI to compare how well UniProt protein records versus the full texts of their cited publications answer biological questions about 50 human kinases. By evaluating information coverage and semantic agreement between AI-generated answers from each source, the study assesses whether curated database annotations capture the same knowledge as the underlying literature. The work offers a scalable approach for auditing annotation completeness and consistency in protein databases.

papers.title: Transformer-based decision support with CNN and ViT for prognostic risk stratification following adjuvant chemotherapy in high-grade glioma: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) exhibit marked intratumoral heterogeneity, which is associated with variable survival outcomes among patients receiving standard adjuvant chemotherapy. Conventional methods relying on molecular biomarkers are constrained by technical limitations and tumor heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop a multi-channel 2.5D deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) features to noninvasively stratify HGG patients based on expected survival outcomes following postoperative adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) chemotherapy a
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This study develops a multi-channel 2.5D deep learning framework combining CNN and Vision Transformer features to noninvasively stratify high-grade glioma patients by expected survival after adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. The approach aims to overcome limitations of conventional molecular biomarkers, which are constrained by technical issues and tumor heterogeneity, using multicenter imaging data.

papers.title: CheckAMG: Accurate Identification of Auxiliary Viral Genes with Genome-Language Models.
papers.abstract: Viruses shape microbial metabolism through auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that reprogram host metabolism, physiology, and gene regulation during infection. Identifying AVGs is complicated by ambiguous viral versus cellular assignment, inconsistent curation, and reliance on sequence homology that misses divergent functions. Here we present CheckAMG, which pairs annotation-based AVG prediction, curated with a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic function, with a finetuned genome-language model for annotation-independent discovery. Benchmarked against DRAM-V and VIBRAN
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CheckAMG is a new tool that identifies auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) by combining annotation-based prediction with a fine-tuned genome-language model, addressing problems of ambiguous viral vs. cellular assignment and reliance on sequence homology. It uses a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic functions, and is benchmarked against existing tools DRAM-V and VIBRAN.

papers.title: DeepNPA: A protBert-based framework for residue-level annotation of neuropeptide precursors.
papers.abstract: Neuropeptides are key signaling molecules that regulate the nervous and endocrine systems, and their maturation depends on precise proteolytic cleavage of precursor proteins. However, residue-level annotation remains essential yet experimentally labor intensive, with limited dedicated computational tools. Here, we present DeepNPA, a residue-level annotation framework that integrates ProtBert, a pretrained protein language model, with focal loss for imbalance-aware optimization. DeepNPA was trained and evaluated on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset annotated using the BIO scheme. On a
papers.summary: DeepNPA is a new computational framework that uses the pretrained protein language model ProtBert, combined with focal loss to handle class imbalance, to annotate neuropeptide precursor proteins at the residue level. It was trained and evaluated on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset using the BIO annotation scheme, aiming to replace labor-intensive experimental annotation. The tool provides a dedicated resource for identifying cleavage sites and neuropeptide regions in precursor sequences.

papers.title: Dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding for anticancer peptide prediction via transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Computational identification of anti-tumor peptides (ACPs) is challenged by limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences. Standard transformer positional encodings fail to capture the periodicities and local motifs that govern peptide function. We propose dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), which replaces fixed sinusoidal encodings with parallel adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches, fused by a context-aware gating mechanism. A dual-stage transfer learning strategy pre-trains on 5,785 curated peptide sequences before fine-tuning on ACP74
papers.summary: The authors introduce dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), a transformer positional encoding scheme that combines adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches via context-aware gating to better capture periodicities and local motifs in peptide sequences. Using a dual-stage transfer learning strategy, they pre-train on 5,785 curated peptides and fine-tune for anticancer peptide prediction, aiming to overcome limited training data and multi-scale sequence features.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: SF-DTI is a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that combines multiple protein encoders, aligns drug structure with semantic representations, and progressively refines cross-modal features. It aims to bridge the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities while better exploiting pretrained encoders. The approach targets improved accuracy in identifying whether a drug binds a given protein target.

papers.title: Predicting Functional Diversity Within Enzyme Families: A Practical Perspective.
papers.abstract: Machine learning has become an increasingly powerful tool in enzyme discovery, enabling the prediction of enzyme activity, substrate scope, and functional specificity across diverse protein families. However, many reported models rely on narrowly sampled datasets and task-specific benchmarks, limiting their robustness and generalizability to distantly related enzymes or novel chemical substrates. In this concept article, we provide a practical, best-practice-oriented perspective on developing enzyme family- or class-specific machine learning (ML) predictors with an emphasis on data quality, re
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This concept article offers practical guidance for building machine learning models that predict enzyme function within specific enzyme families, emphasizing data quality and robust benchmarking. It argues that many existing models are limited by narrow datasets and task-specific benchmarks, which undermines their generalizability to novel substrates or distant homologs. The authors propose best practices for developing more reliable family- or class-specific functional predictors.

papers.title: Machine learning and multi-omics analyses reveal CLDN1 as a candidate marker associated with colorectal cancer invasion and nutlin-3a (-) response.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is molecularly, cellularly and spatially heterogeneous, and current staging systems and biomarkers incompletely explain prognosis and treatment response. This study integrated transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and in vitro experiments to prioritize candidate CRC-associated markers and characterize their potential biological and clinical relevance.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and in vitro experiments to identify CLDN1 as a candidate marker linked to colorectal cancer invasion and response to the drug nutlin-3a. The multi-omics approach prioritizes CLDN1 as a potentially clinically relevant biomarker that may help explain CRC heterogeneity and treatment response beyond current staging systems.

papers.title: Quantifying the impact of genetic mutations on enhancer dynamics.
papers.abstract: Transcriptional regulation is mediated by enhancers, yet how genetic perturbations alter enhancer activity and gene expression remains unclear. We develop UDI-UMI-STARR-seq, integrating dual indexes and unique molecular identifiers, and combine it with RNA-seq to profile perturbation-associated changes in enhancer activity and gene expression. We apply this approach to 253,632 fragments representing 46,142 cell type-specific candidate enhancers and assess the impact of CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of six transcription factors (ATF2, CTCF, FOXA1, LEF1, TCF7L2, and SCRT1). We identify responsiv
papers.summary: The authors developed UDI-UMI-STARR-seq, a method that combines dual indexes and unique molecular identifiers to measure enhancer activity at scale, and paired it with RNA-seq to link genetic perturbations to changes in enhancer function and gene expression. Applying this to over 250,000 enhancer fragments and CRISPR/Cas9 deletion of six transcription factors, they identified enhancers whose activity depends on specific TFs and connected these to downstream transcriptional changes.

papers.title: Network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell analysis, and molecular docking reveal 6PPD/6PPD-Q-associated atrial fibrillation signatures.
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent sustained arrhythmia worldwide, and environmental factors are increasingly recognized as contributors to its complex pathogenesis. The tire antioxidant N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its oxidation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) are emerging environmental contaminants with reported cardiotoxicity; however, their molecular relationship with AF remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell analysis, and molecular docking to investigate how the environmental tire-derived contaminants 6PPD and 6PPD-Q may contribute to atrial fibrillation. The authors identify molecular signatures and potential mechanisms linking these pollutants to AF pathogenesis, suggesting environmental exposure as a previously underappreciated driver of the arrhythmia.

papers.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of Novel STK3/4 Inhibitors with Anti-Obesity Potential.
papers.abstract: Obesity is associated with impaired adipocyte metabolism driven in part by mitochondrial dysfunction. Serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (STK3) and STK4 promote mitophagy, leading to reduced mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue. Thus, inhibition of STK3/4 represents a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity and related metabolic disorders.
papers.summary: The authors developed and tested novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting STK3/4 kinases, which drive mitophagy and reduce mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue. In preclinical models, these inhibitors showed potential as an anti-obesity strategy by preserving mitochondrial function in adipocytes. This represents an early-stage drug discovery effort linking mitophagy regulation to metabolic disease.

papers.title: PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal-Binding Site and Type Prediction.
papers.abstract: Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal-binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best-reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high-resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium-resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, ac
papers.summary: PrOMet is a new deep learning method for predicting where metals bind on proteins and which metal type binds there. It achieves better accuracy than previous tools, especially on lower-resolution structures where earlier methods struggled, addressing a gap in protein-metal interaction prediction.

papers.title: Epigenetic Silencing of CYYR1 Promotes Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression Through TRIM21-Dependent Regulation of HMMR Stability.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Integrative multi-omics and machine-learning analyses across independent cohorts identified CYYR1 as a frequently downregulated transmembrane protein in LUAD, with low expression associated with poor prognosis and promoter hypermethylation. CYYR1 restoration suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, tumor growth, and metastasis. Mechanistically, CYYR1 facilitated TRIM21-dependent ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HMMR, thereby reducing CDC20-associated oncogenic signaling. Biochemical and
papers.summary: This study identifies CYYR1 as a frequently silenced gene in lung adenocarcinoma, where promoter hypermethylation reduces its expression and correlates with poor patient prognosis. Restoring CYYR1 suppresses tumor growth and metastasis by promoting TRIM21-mediated degradation of HMMR, which in turn dampens CDC20-associated oncogenic signaling.

papers.title: Revealing the toxicological effects and mechanisms of tris(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate exposure on osteoarthritis based on network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative disease affecting all joints in the body, impacting over 500 million people globally and imposing a significant healthcare burden. Tris(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCPP), one of the widely used organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs), exhibits notable environmental and biological toxicity. However, the role and molecular mechanisms of TCPP exposure in OA remain unclear. This study combined network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking techniques to identify key targets and pathways associated with TCPP exposure and OA. A nomogram model was
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking to identify key targets and pathways linking exposure to the flame retardant TCPP with osteoarthritis. The authors construct a nomogram model to predict TCPP-related OA risk and highlight candidate molecular mechanisms. The work suggests environmental pollutant exposure may contribute to OA pathogenesis through specific target genes and pathways.

papers.title: Machine-learning model for distinguishing cytomegalovirus infection status in hospitalised patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: a retrospective cohort study with temporal validation.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study developed and temporally validated a machine-learning model to distinguish cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection status in hospitalized patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The model uses routinely available clinical and laboratory data to identify CMV infection, potentially enabling earlier diagnosis and treatment in this high-risk population. Temporal validation supports its potential clinical utility, though prospective confirmation is needed.

papers.title: Massively Multiplexed Photonic Chip With Cross-Channel Fusion For Harmonized Biosensing.
papers.abstract: Accurate, label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures is limited by poor multiplexing scalability and inconsistent responses across sensor samples. We introduce a transformative sensing platform that integrates large-scale photonic multiplexing with data-driven analytics to overcome these constraints. Our modular, affordable glass-chip whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) photonic architecture is designed to support simultaneous readout of up to 100 sensing channels comprising over 10 000 high-Q microresonators, exceeding existing multiplexing capabilities by more than two orders of magnitude.
papers.summary: The authors present a glass-chip photonic sensing platform based on whispering-gallery-mode microresonators that can read out up to 100 sensing channels containing over 10,000 high-Q resonators simultaneously, a multiplexing scale more than 100-fold beyond existing biosensors. They pair this hardware with data-driven cross-channel fusion analytics to harmonize inconsistent responses across sensor elements, enabling accurate label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures.

papers.title: A self-supervised foundation model for large-scale zebrafish image analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput zebrafish screening generates large volumes of imaging data, creating a need for scalable computational methods that reduce dependence on manual annotation and repeated task-specific model development. In this study, we develop a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis pretrained on more than 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous zebrafish imaging datasets spanning different developmental stages, imaging platforms, modalities, and experimental conditions. By learning a shared representation from diverse unlabeled zebrafish images, the proposed framework
papers.summary: The authors developed a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis, pretrained on over 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous imaging datasets covering different developmental stages, platforms, and modalities. This shared representation aims to reduce reliance on manual annotation and task-specific model development for high-throughput zebrafish screening.

papers.title: Examining Protein Residue-Level Stability Using Theory and Experiment.
papers.abstract: Protein behavior, whether evolved in nature or intentionally designed, is governed by the energetics of amino acid interactions that bridge sequence to function. As an extension of the theory of protein folding funnels, local frustration quantifies the optimality of these residue-level interactions relative to alternatives. Although this framework has existed for decades, experimental validation has remained elusive. Past deep mutational scanning datasets enable experimental assessment across nearly 8,000 positions from 178 proteins. Results provide experimental evidence for theoretical predic
papers.summary: This study provides experimental validation of the local frustration framework, which quantifies how optimal residue-level interactions are in protein structures. Using deep mutational scanning data covering nearly 8,000 positions across 178 proteins, the authors show that theoretically predicted frustration correlates with experimental mutational effects. This bridges a long-standing gap between protein folding theory and measurable sequence-structure-function relationships.

papers.title: ParaEM: Antigen-aware sequence-based paratope prediction with Expectation-Maximization.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of antibody paratopes-the residues contacting the antigen-is vital for understanding antibody-antigen recognition, antibody engineering, and vaccine design. However, structure-based predictors require antibody structural inputs, which are often obtained from experimentally determined antibody-antigen complexes in benchmark settings but are generally unavailable for new sequences. Conversely, sequence-based predictors scale efficiently but remain largely antigen-agnostic, limiting their use of pair-specific antigen context.
papers.summary: ParaEM is a new sequence-based method for predicting antibody paratopes (the residues that contact antigen) that incorporates antigen context, unlike prior sequence-based tools that are largely antigen-agnostic. It uses an Expectation-Maximization framework to make antigen-aware predictions directly from sequence, avoiding the need for antibody structural inputs required by structure-based predictors.

papers.title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning.
papers.abstract: Proteins are the main drivers of cell function and disease, making proteomics a powerful technique for biomarker discovery and defining cell identity. While current technologies can profile thousands of proteins and reach single-cell sensitivity, limited throughput restricts applications such as robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts. To close this gap, we present a deep-learning (DL) approach for the direct analysis of mass spectrometric (MS) data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity. Specifically, we introduce the ProFormer, a transformer pipeline that clas
papers.summary: ProFormer is a transformer-based deep learning pipeline that directly classifies mass spectrometry proteomic profiles, assigning samples to their biological or clinical identity without requiring extensive preprocessing. It is designed to work on both single-cell and plasma proteomes, addressing throughput limitations in large cohort classification. The approach demonstrates generalizability across different proteomic data types.

papers.title: Agentic campaign control for high-throughput de novo binder design.
papers.abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence has produced a rapidly growing ecosystem of methods for de novo protein design. With access to many specialized and often complementary tools, how does one use them effectively, especially with a finite compute budget? Here, we introduce Target-adaptive Rescue-Explore-eXploit (T-REX) , an agentic protein binder design framework that orchestrates multiple state-of-the-art protein generative models and structure evaluators. Over the course of a design campaign, T-REX leverages large language model (LLM) agents to reason over accumulating outcomes and decide wh
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: T-REX is an agentic framework that uses LLM agents to orchestrate multiple protein generative models and structure evaluators for de novo binder design, adaptively deciding which tools to run as results accumulate. It aims to make high-throughput binder design campaigns more effective under finite compute budgets by reasoning over outcomes and balancing exploration and exploitation.

papers.title: pLM-HP: Peptide hormone prediction using pre-trained protein language model representations.
papers.abstract: Peptide hormones play key roles in metabolic regulation, growth and development, and the maintenance of homeostasis and are important targets for drug discovery and design. However, traditional experimental methods for screening and identifying peptide hormones are costly and inefficient. Although existing machine learning methods have made some progress, they pay limited attention to class imbalance, and there is still room to improve prediction performance.
papers.summary: The paper introduces pLM-HP, a machine learning method that uses representations from a pre-trained protein language model to predict peptide hormones. It explicitly addresses class imbalance, a common problem in this prediction task, and reports improved performance over existing methods. The tool aims to speed up identification of peptide hormones relevant to drug discovery.

papers.title: Moran's index habitat and peritumoral radiomics based on digital breast tomosynthesis for predicting Ki-67 status in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: The heterogeneity of breast cancer is a key factor influencing treatment decisions and patient prognosis. As a crucial cell proliferation marker, the expression level of the Ki-67 protein is closely associated with tumor aggressiveness, recurrence risk, and prognosis. The goal of this study was to develop and validate an integrated radiomics model based on digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) that incorporates both habitat subregions and peritumoral features to preoperatively predict Ki-67 expression status in breast cancer.
papers.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
papers.summary: This study develops a radiomics model using digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) imaging that combines habitat subregion analysis (via Moran's index) with peritumoral features to predict Ki-67 expression status in breast cancer preoperatively. The integrated model aims to improve non-invasive assessment of tumor proliferation, which is linked to aggressiveness and prognosis.

papers.title: A Dynamics-Informed Machine Learning Framework for Inhibitor Optimization Against Quickly Evolving Targets to Avoid Resistance.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance often emerges through mutations that reshape protein conformational ensembles, allowing inhibitor potency to be altered without directly disrupting protein-ligand contacts. Consequently, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain difficult to identify, hindering the design of inhibitors with durable potency against rapidly evolving drug targets. To address this challenge, we developed ROBUST, a physics-informed machine learning framework that integrates experimental measurements, molecular dynamics simulations, and interpretable statistical modeling to identify en
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present ROBUST, a physics-informed machine learning framework that combines experimental measurements, molecular dynamics simulations, and interpretable statistical modeling to identify how resistance mutations reshape protein conformational ensembles and alter inhibitor potency. This approach aims to guide the design of inhibitors with durable potency against rapidly evolving drug targets.

papers.title: Screening for patients at risk for cardiac amyloidosis via electronic health records: A multicenter machine learning development and validation study.
papers.abstract: Timely detection is crucial to improve outcomes in patients with cardiac amyloidosis (CA) by initiation of guideline-directed disease-modifying treatments. Although confirmatory bone scintigraphy is highly accurate for CA detection, identifying at-risk patients for referral remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model, Amylo-Detect, using structured multimodal electronic health record (EHR) data to guide referrals for confirmatory scintigraphy and monoclonal protein testing. Consecutive all-comer patients (n = 11,616) referred for bone scintigraphy at
papers.summary: This study developed and validated a machine learning model, Amylo-Detect, that uses structured multimodal electronic health record data to identify patients at risk for cardiac amyloidosis who should be referred for confirmatory bone scintigraphy and monoclonal protein testing. Across a multicenter cohort of 11,616 patients referred for bone scintigraphy, the model aims to improve timely detection and enable earlier initiation of disease-modifying treatments.

papers.title: Empathy in the Soil, Agents on the Desktop: Why Plant Pathology Needs a Scientist-in-the-Loop AI Paradigm.
papers.abstract: Plant pathology faces a cognitive bottleneck caused by the growing volume of biological data. Addressing it requires a shift from passive chatbots to autonomous AI research agents that operate in Goal-Action-State cycles. Researchers can set up a local, desktop-based agentic framework that combines semantic discovery, LLM-Wiki knowledge synthesis, and in silico prevalidation, managed under a human-directed three-tier organizational model. Strict "Scientist-in-the-Loop" boundaries, which means that a human researcher sets the goals, reviews AI-generated output before it is treated as evidence,
papers.summary: This perspective article argues that plant pathology faces a data-driven cognitive bottleneck that passive chatbots cannot solve, and proposes instead autonomous AI research agents operating in Goal-Action-State cycles. The authors outline a local, desktop-based agentic framework combining semantic discovery, LLM-Wiki knowledge synthesis, and in silico prevalidation, governed by a human-directed three-tier organizational model with strict 'Scientist-in-the-Loop' boundaries. The core claim is that human researchers must set goals and review AI output before it is treated as evidence.

papers.title: Omics data discovery agents: Agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g., protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs lar
papers.summary: The authors present an agentic framework that autonomously retrieves, reanalyzes, and synthesizes published omics data from the biomedical literature, addressing the problem that most published omics data remain inaccessible for computational reuse. The system uses LLM-based agents to locate dispersed information across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and to handle irregularly shared intermediate data files. This enables scalable reuse and meta-analysis of existing omics studies.

papers.title: Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks Decision Transformer: A Novel Approach for Multi-Objective De Novo Drug Design.
papers.abstract: Designing novel molecules that simultaneously satisfy several, often conflicting, properties is a long-standing challenge in drug design. While recent deep learning advances optimize single targets effectively, navigating the trade-offs required for multiple objectives remains a difficult problem.
papers.summary: The authors propose the Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks Decision Transformer (MOC-RB-DT), a novel deep learning architecture for de novo drug design that can simultaneously optimize multiple, often conflicting molecular properties. The approach extends decision transformer methods by conditioning on return blocks to navigate trade-offs between objectives, addressing a key limitation of prior single-target optimization models.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of mitochondrial proteomes across the tree of life.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria arose from the endosymbiosis of a bacterium with an archaea-related host cell about 2 billion years ago. To understand their origins and evolution, we compared experimentally defined mitoproteomes from the MitoCarta Tree of Life project. Across eight organisms, we identified 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins within 3,199 families, of which 43% lack Pfam domains. We report 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens yet absent in humans, representing promising candidate targets for protozoan infectious diseases. Leveraging our experimentally defined mitoproteomes, we
papers.summary: This study compares experimentally defined mitochondrial proteomes across eight organisms spanning the tree of life, identifying 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins in 3,199 families, with 43% lacking known Pfam domains. The authors highlight 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens but absent in humans, offering potential drug targets for protozoan diseases. The work provides a broad evolutionary view of mitochondrial protein composition and function.

papers.title: ELE: Estimating tissue-specific long noncoding RNA gene essentiality using graph neural networks.
papers.abstract: A gene is essential if its loss of function results in lethality, reduced fitness, or disease. Essential genes have attracted increasing attention due to their vital functions in biological systems. Many efforts have been made to find essential protein-coding genes. In complex organisms, the majority of the genome does not encode proteins. Noncoding genes play vital roles in many biological processes. Investigating the essentiality of noncoding genes is necessary. We present ELE (estimating long noncoding RNA essentiality), the first computational model for finding essential long noncoding RNA
papers.summary: ELE is the first computational model for predicting the essentiality of long noncoding RNA genes, using graph neural networks to estimate tissue-specific essentiality. It addresses a gap in essentiality research, which has largely focused on protein-coding genes despite noncoding genes playing vital roles in biological processes.

papers.title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial mortality and economic losses without science-based interventions. Conventional approaches to combating AMR have important limitations in addressing this escalating threat. Recent advances in AI, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, provide new opportunities to integrate multimodal data for AMR research. However, evidence remains uneven, with many approaches limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. Here, we critically review AI
papers.summary: This review critically examines how artificial intelligence—including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models—can integrate multimodal data to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights that while AI offers promising new avenues for AMR research, much of the current evidence remains limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation.

papers.title: Association between dietary branched-chain amino acid intake and anaemia risk in children and adolescents: a matched case-control study.
papers.abstract: Anaemia in children and adolescents is multifactorial, and evidence on dietary amino-acid intake in relation to anaemia remains limited. This study examined the association between dietary branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) intake and haemoglobin (Hb)-defined anaemia among Chinese children and adolescents using data from the 2016-2019 China Children and Lactating Women Nutrition and Health Survey. Among 11,134 eligible participants aged 6-17 years, quantile g-computation and the Boruta algorithm were first used to screen 20 dietary amino acids. A 1:4 propensity score-matched sample was then cons
papers.summary: This matched case-control study examined whether dietary branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) intake is associated with anaemia risk in Chinese children and adolescents aged 6-17, using data from a large national nutrition survey. The authors used quantile g-computation and the Boruta algorithm to screen 20 dietary amino acids before propensity score matching. The findings suggest a potential link between BCAA intake and haemoglobin-defined anaemia, though the study is observational and cannot establish causality.

papers.title: Immune-related molecular links between asthma and Alzheimer's disease identified by multi-omics, machine learning and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Epidemiological evidence suggests that asthma increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet their shared immune-related molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify immune-associated molecular links between the two diseases.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data, machine learning, and single-cell analysis to uncover shared immune-related molecular mechanisms linking asthma and Alzheimer's disease. The authors identify immune-associated genes and pathways that may explain the epidemiological association between the two conditions, highlighting potential common therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Association and discriminative value of insulin resistance surrogate markers for aortic stiffness in asymptomatic adults.
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance surrogate markers, including the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, TyG-BMI, and TG/HDL-C ratio, have been associated with aortic stiffness in high-risk populations. Their comparative associations and incremental discrimination in asymptomatic adults remain unclear. We therefore compared these markers and evaluated a simplified model for cfPWV-defined aortic stiffness.
papers.summary: This study compares three insulin resistance surrogate markers (TyG index, TyG-BMI, and TG/HDL-C ratio) for their association with aortic stiffness, measured by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity, in asymptomatic adults. It also evaluates whether a simplified model using these markers can improve discrimination of aortic stiffness beyond conventional risk factors.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of graph neural networks and classical machine learning for carbapenem-resistance prediction and genomic interpretation in Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii is a hospital-associated pathogen linked to high mortality and limited treatment options. Although many resistance determinants have been identified, how they organize into coordinated systems remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study compares graph neural networks with classical machine learning methods for predicting carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii and for interpreting the underlying genomic features. It aims to clarify how known resistance determinants organize into coordinated systems rather than acting in isolation. The work offers a methodological benchmark for applying GNNs to antimicrobial resistance prediction.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning characterize LTA4H-linked lipid metabolism and inflammatory signatures in the knee osteoarthritis IPFP/synovium compartment.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a whole-joint disease characterized by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and metabolic imbalance. To define lipid metabolism-related transcriptional heterogeneity within the infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP)/synovium compartment, we integrated publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from IPFP/synovium-derived joint cells with bulk synovial transcriptomic datasets from patients with KOA and controls. Lipid metabolism-related scores were derived using multiple single-cell scoring algorithms, and candidate genes were identified through score-associated analyse
papers.summary: This study integrates public single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data from knee osteoarthritis patients to characterize lipid metabolism-related heterogeneity in the infrapatellar fat pad/synovium compartment. Using multiple single-cell scoring algorithms and machine learning, the authors identify LTA4H-linked lipid metabolism and inflammatory signatures as candidate features of KOA pathology.

papers.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
papers.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melti
papers.summary: The study reports a computation-guided workflow to improve the thermostability of Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a fungal sweet protein with poor intrinsic stability that limits its use in processed foods. Using the newly solved HTS crystal structure, the authors combined Rosetta (physics-based) and ThermoMPNN (deep-learning) predictions to design single-mutant variants, which were experimentally validated to yield improved melting temperatures.

papers.title: Photonic AI for deeper understanding of the Planck epoch.
papers.abstract: This article addresses the requirements for a photonic artificial intelligence (AI) capable of supporting a deeper understanding of the Planck epoch in the origin of the Universe. The article continues the previous author's articles, which outlined requirements for AI to support studies of protein evolution on Earth, cosmic strings (CS) detection, and a non-standard view on the photon's nature. Modern digital generative AI cannot support its solution due to a lack of training datasets and limited energy resources for conducting adequate physical experiments. This article analyses the states of
papers.summary: This opinion piece argues that current digital generative AI is inadequate for studying the Planck epoch of the early Universe because of missing training data and prohibitive energy costs, and proposes photonic AI as a potential alternative. It is a conceptual, speculative continuation of the author's prior work on AI for protein evolution and cosmic string detection, rather than a report of new experimental or computational results.

papers.title: A palmitoylation-associated three-gene signature predicts prognosis, immune features, and drug sensitivity in gastric cancer: functional validation of CTHRC1.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a heterogeneous malignancy that requires improved molecular tools for prognostic stratification. Protein palmitoylation regulates membrane localization and signaling, but the clinical relevance of palmitoylation-related genes (PRGs) in GC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study develops a three-gene prognostic signature based on palmitoylation-related genes to stratify gastric cancer patients by survival, immune features, and drug sensitivity. The authors functionally validate CTHRC1 as a key gene in the signature, linking protein palmitoylation to gastric cancer progression. The work suggests palmitoylation-related genes could serve as clinical biomarkers for prognosis and treatment selection in gastric cancer.

papers.title: Benchmarking ensemble and deep learning models for drought-responsive gene prioritisation in rice using multi-omics data.
papers.abstract: Identifying drought-responsive genes is critical for climate-resilient crop breeding, yet computational gene-trait association often relies on single-omics or generalized genomic datasets. Optimal algorithm selection for high-dimensional, small multi-omics datasets also remains a persistent challenge. We present a machine learning framework that extends the QTG-Finder feature set by integrating transcriptomic and proteomic features to classify drought-responsive genes in rice. Using MBKBase annotations, we evaluated the ability of these models to prioritise 336 drought-responsive genes among 2
papers.summary: This study builds a machine learning framework that extends the QTG-Finder feature set by adding transcriptomic and proteomic features to classify drought-responsive genes in rice. Using MBKBase annotations, the authors benchmark ensemble and deep learning models on a small, high-dimensional multi-omics dataset to prioritize 336 drought-responsive genes. The work highlights the challenge of optimal algorithm selection for such datasets and offers a comparative assessment of model performance.

papers.title: Lightweight 2D-Convolutional Neural Network for Drug-Kinase Binding Affinity Prediction with Minimal Encoded Representations.
papers.abstract: Drug-kinase binding affinity (DKBA) prediction plays a crucial role in prioritizing compounds and reducing the time and financial resources required for drug discovery. However, many existing deep learning models rely on complex molecular representations, such as molecular graphs or pretrained embeddings, which may increase computational complexity and limit scalability.
papers.journal: Iranian journal of pharmaceutical research : IJPR
papers.summary: This paper introduces a lightweight 2D-convolutional neural network for predicting drug-kinase binding affinity, using minimal encoded molecular representations instead of complex graphs or pretrained embeddings. The approach aims to reduce computational complexity and improve scalability while maintaining useful predictive performance for compound prioritization in drug discovery.

papers.title: Integrated network toxicology and multi-omics profiling reveal cell cycle, DNA damage repair, and metabolic alterations in cyclophosphamide-induced premature ovarian insufficiency.
papers.abstract: Cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced chemotherapy injury is a leading iatrogenic cause of premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) and a major barrier to fertility preservation. Yet the systems-level mechanisms underlying its reproductive toxicity remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study combines network toxicology with multi-omics profiling to investigate how cyclophosphamide causes premature ovarian insufficiency. The authors identify disruptions in cell cycle regulation, DNA damage repair, and metabolic pathways as key mechanisms underlying the reproductive toxicity.

papers.title: ZBP1 contributes to IFN-β-induced PANoptosis-related skeletal muscle cell injury in dermatomyositis.
papers.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by cutaneous manifestations and inflammatory skeletal muscle injury. Dysregulated type I interferon signaling and regulated cell death pathways may converge to promote myofiber damage. PANoptosis integrates core components of pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, but its contribution to DM remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether ZBP1, a nucleic acid sensor, mediates a form of inflammatory cell death called PANoptosis in skeletal muscle cells during dermatomyositis. The authors propose that IFN-β signaling drives ZBP1-dependent PANoptosis, contributing to muscle fiber damage in this autoimmune disease. The findings suggest a potential mechanistic link between type I interferon dysregulation and regulated cell death in DM pathology.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning models for predicting New-onset acute organ injury within 48 hours of admission in patients with community-acquired acute cholangitis.
papers.abstract: Community-acquired acute cholangitis (CAAC) can progress to acute organ injury (AOI), increasing poor prognosis risk. This study aimed to develop machine learning models using clinical information obtained before AOI onset to predict new-onset AOI within 48 h after admission in patients with CAAC.
papers.summary: This study develops machine learning models that use routinely collected clinical data available at admission to predict which patients with community-acquired acute cholangitis will develop new acute organ injury within 48 hours. The models aim to support earlier risk stratification and clinical decision-making in this patient population.

papers.title: RCSB PDB AI Help Desk: retrieval-augmented generation for protein structure deposition support.
papers.abstract: Structural biologists have contributed more than 260 000 experimentally determined three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules to the Protein Data Bank. Incoming depositions are validated and biocurated by approximately 20 expert biocurators at the collaborating data centers worldwide. Biocurators at the Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics Protein Data Bank, who process more than 40% of global depositions, face growing difficulty sustaining efficient Help Desk operations, having received roughly 19 000 depositor messages across some 8000 entries in 2025.
papers.summary: The RCSB PDB has developed an AI Help Desk that uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to assist structural biologists with depositing their structures into the Protein Data Bank. The system aims to ease the burden on expert biocurators, who handle roughly 19,000 depositor messages across 8,000 entries annually. This represents a practical application of LLM-based RAG to scientific data curation workflows.

papers.title: An evidence-weighted knowledge framework with path-aware reasoning for personalized lifestyle management in chronic disease.
papers.abstract: Healthy lifestyle management is essential for chronic disease prevention and long-term care. However, evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes is dispersed across diverse biomedical sources. This fragmentation makes it difficult for health professionals to efficiently retrieve and interpret evidence needed to inform personalized lifestyle guidance.
papers.summary: The authors propose an evidence-weighted knowledge framework that integrates fragmented biomedical evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes, using path-aware reasoning to support personalized lifestyle management for chronic disease. The goal is to help health professionals more efficiently retrieve and interpret relevant evidence for tailored lifestyle guidance.

papers.title: Multi-omics graph attention network reveals neuro-immune-tumor pathways in breast cancer liver depression syndrome.
papers.abstract: Liver depression syndrome (LDS) is a core Chinese medicine (CM) syndrome implicated in the onset and progression of breast cancer, whose molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering further investigation.
papers.summary: This study applies a multi-omics graph attention network to investigate the molecular mechanisms linking liver depression syndrome (LDS), a core Chinese medicine syndrome, to breast cancer progression. The approach integrates multiple omics layers to identify neuro-immune-tumor pathways associated with LDS in breast cancer. The findings suggest that LDS-related molecular signatures involve crosstalk between neural, immune, and tumor systems.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified human-mouse shared gene space and uses supervised contrastive learning to infer gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq data. It models gene-cell expression relationships via a multi-relational heterograph to predict transcription factor-target regulatory interactions, addressing noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts.

papers.title: Radiomics and deep learning for immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes: imaging-derived immune phenotyping and clinical translation across solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of multiple solid tumors, but durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients and conventional size-based imaging does not fully capture immune-related response patterns. Radiomics and deep learning offer a route to convert routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT into quantitative biomarkers of tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and temporal treatment response. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence across solid tumors with an emphasis on four questions that are often separated in the literature: what
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on using radiomics and deep learning to predict immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes across solid tumors, framing imaging as a tool for non-invasive immune phenotyping. It emphasizes four interconnected questions often treated separately in the literature, covering tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and temporal treatment response from routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT. The review aims to bridge imaging-derived biomarkers with clinical translation for ICI patient selection and monitoring.

papers.title: Explainable growth stage classification of cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) leaves and key feature visualization using vision transformer and transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate and objective plant phenotyping is crucial for optimizing agricultural practices, understanding plant development, and enabling rapid responses to environmental changes. Traditional methods, often relying on visual observation, can be subjective, time-consuming, and may overlook subtle but important differences. This study demonstrates the power of combining digital imaging with deep learning to classify plant material with high accuracy, even when visual differences are minimal. We focused on differentiating between stage D (light green) and stage E (dark green) leaves of cacao (Theo
papers.summary: This study applies a vision transformer with transfer learning to classify cacao leaves into two developmental stages (D and E) based on subtle color differences, achieving high accuracy where human visual assessment is subjective. The authors also visualize key features driving the model's decisions, improving interpretability of the deep learning pipeline for plant phenotyping.

papers.title: Exploring the key genes of colorectal "adenoma-cancer" based on graph transformer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, and the precise identification of biomarkers from colonic adenoma to cancer is of great significance for preventing the development of adenocarcinoma. Given that existing methods inadequately capture the topological network relationships among genes, this study proposes a graph neural network model based on multifeature learning, named ChebTs, to investigate the correlation between key genes involved in the colorectal "adenoma-cancer" transition. The GSE41657 and GSE31905 datasets from the GEO database were stratified in
papers.summary: This study introduces ChebTs, a graph transformer-based neural network that integrates multiple gene features to identify key genes driving the transition from colorectal adenoma to cancer. Using GEO datasets GSE41657 and GSE31905, the model aims to better capture topological gene network relationships than existing methods, potentially improving biomarker discovery for early CRC prevention.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Stem Cell Research: From Biological Data to Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Stem cell (SC) research plays a central role in disease modeling and regenerative medicine, yet its clinical translation remains challenged by biological heterogeneity, incomplete cellular maturation, stringent quality-control requirements, and increasingly complex biological and clinical data. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for extracting biologically meaningful information from these data, enabling quantitative characterization of SC behavior and predictive modeling across diverse experimental and translational applications. This review presents a unif
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across stem cell research, from analyzing complex biological data to supporting clinical translation. It highlights how ML helps address challenges like cellular heterogeneity, incomplete maturation, and quality control in regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Bio-Inspired Artificial Intelligence Multimorbidity Score for Human-Machine Clinical Risk Stratification.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity is strongly associated with mortality, but existing comorbidity indices often generalize poorly across populations because they depend on fixed disease lists and context-specific weights. We developed the large-language-model-based multimorbidity score (LLM-MMS), a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity phenotype score, as a bio-inspired artificial intelligence score for human-machine clinical risk stratification and evaluated it for all-cause mortality prediction in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts. Harmonized participant-level data wer
papers.summary: The authors developed LLM-MMS, a prompt-based large language model-derived multimorbidity score, and evaluated it for predicting all-cause mortality in 770,439 adults across 9 international longitudinal cohorts. The score aims to overcome the poor generalizability of traditional fixed-disease-list comorbidity indices by using a bio-inspired AI approach for human-machine clinical risk stratification.
